author: product-requirements-expert
title: Filter the veterinarian directory by specialty
summary: Both the human-readable veterinarian page and the reinstated machine-readable list can be narrowed to the vets holding one named specialty via a request parameter (no on-page control). Whole-name, case-insensitive match; filtered paging carries the parameter across pages.
acceptance_criteria: Requesting the HTML directory naming a held specialty lists only the vets holding it, a page at a time
Filtered HTML pagination links carry the specialty so the narrowing holds when moving between pages
Requesting the machine-readable (JSON) list naming a held specialty returns only the vets holding it
The specialty is matched in full and case-insensitively, not as a prefix, on both surfaces
A specialty no vet holds returns the surface's normal successful response (HTTP 200) with an empty vet list, not an error
An empty or whitespace-only specialty value is treated as absent, matching the empty-owner-search behavior, on both surfaces
With no specialty named, both surfaces behave exactly as they do today
A vet holding more than one specialty is included when any one of them is the named specialty
non_goals: A visible page control (form or dropdown) for the specialty filter
notes: Narrows NG-9 (free-text vet search stays out; specialty filtering in) per adr/2026-08-08-non-goal-vet-free-text-search.md. Reinstates the /vets JSON endpoint as a supported surface; this filter is its first requested capability. REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn and its ID is not reused; the Superseded entry and the removed 'carries no requirement' known-defect edge case were corrected. Docs/adr/README.md index needs a row for the new non-goal ADR added by the ADR-index owner (outside product-requirements-expert write scope).

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The slice extends the existing declarative-repository + controller-paging idiom (VetController and VetRepository, system-design Contracts) with an optional specialty filter, mirroring the OwnerController/OwnerRepository search-and-page pattern. It adds two derived query methods on VetRepository (whole-name, case-insensitive via the IgnoreCase keyword, not a prefix), an optional request parameter on each of the two existing vet routes using the same blank/whitespace-as-absent branch OwnerController applies to lastName, and template page links that carry the parameter. No new module, no new pattern, no new dependency. The scope decision is already recorded in the pre-existing non-goal ADR; I added its missing README index row. Hence minor, not new.
integration_points: VetRepository gains a paged method returning Page<Vet> for the HTML surface and a Collection<Vet> method for the JSON surface, both filtering on Vet.specialties -> Specialty.name with the IgnoreCase keyword for a whole-name case-insensitive match

VetController.showVetList and showResourcesVetList each gain an optional specialty request parameter; null/blank/whitespace strips to absent and calls the existing findAll, a non-blank value (stripped) calls the filtered method
VetController adds the specialty to the HTML model so vetList.html page links can carry it across pages

patterns.description: null-guard + strip + blank-as-broadest branch and paged-result assembly to mirror for the specialty parameter

declarative derived query returning Page<T>; use the IgnoreCase keyword for whole-name case-insensitive match, NOT StartingWith, which would be a prefix and violates the not-a-prefix acceptance criterion

risks.risk: vetList.html page links use string-concatenation hrefs that cannot carry a second parameter cleanly and would not URL-encode the specialty
risks.mitigation: switch the page-link expressions to Thymeleaf URL-building syntax that takes page and specialty as parameters (encodes correctly); given blank-as-absent, an empty value in the link is harmless, but prefer omitting the parameter when absent

risks.risk: annotating the new filtered methods Cacheable on the vets cache adds one cache entry per distinct specialty string (case variants included) and the cache has no eviction (Open Question 5)
risks.mitigation: consistent with the no-write-path posture and bounded by the small specialty set; acceptable, or leave the filtered methods uncached since the base collection is already cached and tiny

risks.risk: a ManyToMany join could in principle yield duplicate Vet rows
risks.mitigation: a vet holds at most one specialty of a given name, so an exact-name match returns at most one row per vet; findDistinct is available if the implementer wants belt-and-braces

notes: Added the index row for docs/adr/2026-08-08-non-goal-vet-free-text-search.md to docs/adr/README.md, the item handed off as outside product-requirements-expert write scope. No new architectural ADR: whole-name-vs-prefix and case-insensitivity are product decisions already fixed in the PRD acceptance criteria, and the scope decision is captured in the existing non-goal ADR. Trust boundary: specialty is a query parameter already inside the Threat Model SQL-injection row (parameterized derived query) and XSS row (Thymeleaf auto-escapes and URL-encodes); no new boundary, blank fails safe to the full list, and a no-match returns HTTP 200 with an empty list with no error-detail leakage. Post-implementation doc-sync should add REQ-VET-003 to the VetController and VetRepository Implements cells in system-design Contracts and reclassify the Known Defects row stating the machine-readable route serves no requirement, since /vets is now a supported surface under REQ-VET-003 (REQ-VET-002 withdrawn) and no longer pending removal; left to doc-sync as it tracks landed code.

findings.description: The PRD acceptance criterion 'A specialty no vet holds returns the surface's normal successful response (HTTP 200) with an empty vet list, not an error' explicitly covers both surfaces, but unmatchedSpecialtyShouldReturnEmptyDirectoryWithSuccess only tests the HTML surface (/vets.html?specialty=unicorn-care). The JSON surface (/vets?specialty=nonexistent) is untested at the controller level. In the mock context, an unstubbed findBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase call returns null by default; addAll(null) on the Vets list would throw NullPointerException rather than returning 200 + empty list, so this gap may also mask a latent NPE if the mock default surfaces first.
findings.fix: Add a test jsonDirectoryShouldReturnEmptyListForUnmatchedSpecialty that stubs findBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase("unicorn-care") to return an empty collection, then performs GET /vets?specialty=unicorn-care and asserts status 200, content-type JSON, and $.vetList size 0.

findings.description: blankSpecialtyShouldBehaveAsNoFilter contains two mockMvc.perform calls covering two distinct surfaces (HTML at line 143, JSON at line 147). The testing brief (§ Four-Phase Test Structure) requires one logical assertion per test; testing both surfaces in a single method conflates two behaviors and makes the failure message ambiguous.
findings.fix: Split into blankSpecialtyShouldBehaveAsNoFilterOnHtml (line 143 perform + assert) and blankSpecialtyShouldBehaveAsNoFilterOnJson (line 147 perform + assert).

findings.description: specialtyFilterShouldMatchWholeNameCaseInsensitivelyAndNotOnPrefix contains three act/assert cycles (exact match, upper-case match, prefix non-match) in a single test method. The testing brief (§ Parameterized Tests checklist, § Test Structure) calls for @ParameterizedTest for repetitive cases and one logical behavior per test. A future failure will not identify which case broke without reading the stack trace.
findings.fix: Split into three tests or use @ParameterizedTest with a source that names each case: exact-match, case-insensitive-match, and prefix-non-match. Expected results differ per case, so a @MethodSource or three separate @Test methods are both acceptable.
